title: Latent Knowledge + Behavioral Safety Evals: The Representation Gap Compounds

original_idea.title: Latent Knowledge + Behavioral Safety Evals: The Representation Gap Compounds
original_idea.problem: If safety evaluations test behavioral outputs but dangerous latent knowledge persists in representations, AND if post-training alignment methods suppress behavior without removing knowledge, the compound failure is: model passes behavioral evals, appears safe, gets deployed, and latent knowledge is later elicited.
original_idea.direction: On open-source models, compare behavioral safety eval scores, representation probe scores for dangerous knowledge, and scores after lightweight adversarial fine-tuning. Test whether models with high behavioral safety scores but detectable dangerous latent representations are more susceptible to safety degradation via adversarial fine-tuning.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If behavioral evals and representational probes give discordant safety signals, behavioral evals alone are insufficient for deployment decisions.
original_idea.relevant_context: RLHF is known to suppress but not remove dangerous capabilities (Hubinger et al. 'sleeper agents' work). Representation probing is accessible with basic ML skills and a single GPU.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling: addresses a critical gap where behavioral evals give false confidence. Clear chain from discordant signals to improved deployment decisions. Independent value in the representation probing methodology itself.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Representation probing is accessible with basic ML skills and a single GPU as noted. However, combining probing with adversarial fine-tuning and behavioral eval comparison is intermediate complexity requiring mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three-part comparison (behavioral, probing, post-fine-tuning) requires sustained effort but is feasible with a single model and narrow topic. Could deliver a focused first result within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Hubinger et al. 'Sleeper Agents' (arxiv 2401.05566) demonstrated deceptive behaviors persisting through safety training. Anthropic's 'Simple probes can catch sleeper agents' showed linear probes achieve >99% AUROC detecting when sleeper agents will defect. The specific three-way comparison (behavioral evals vs. representation probes vs. post-adversarial-fine-tuning) is partially addressed: probing for latent knowledge is established, and fine-tuning safety degradation is documented (arxiv 2506.17209, ICLR 2024 paper on fine-tuning compromising alignment). The compound framing adds incremental novelty but the core components are largely covered.
